ops.title: Codex support across capt-hook and the cc-* ecosystem
ops.body:
# Codex support across capt-hook and the cc-* ecosystem

## Context

Support local Codex CLI, the desktop app, and Codex terminals inside Orca. Keep capt-hook’s familiar authoring API, install reusable plugins globally, and retain monorepo-specific policy in `~/Code/monorepo`. cc-present must deliver interactive feedback to both active and idle Codex threads.

Codex already provides native hooks for blocking and rewriting local tool calls, including calls nested inside code mode. cc-transcript already parses Codex; its missing pieces are current execution telemetry, incremental normalization, and integration with consumers. [Codex hooks](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)

Defaults: preserve existing Claude behavior and stored data; use a shared local Codex server; exclude hosted Codex, Orca native chat, and public plugin-directory submission.

## Approach

1. **Establish matching source baselines and a migration inventory.**
   - Work from source revisions matching installed dependencies. capt-hook pins cc-transcript **14.19.0**; the current local cc-transcript checkout is **14.9.0**.
   - Obtain missing plugin source checkouts and preserve unrelated working-copy changes. Never modify installed plugin caches.
   - Track all 28 enabled Claude plugin identities, their dependencies, Codex equivalents, and acceptance checks. Keep durable implementation records in cc-notes.

2. **Complete cc-transcript’s shared execution model.**
   - Normalize Codex command, patch, MCP, subagent, and token telemetry in Rust. Preserve arbitrary code-mode JavaScript as opaque source; derive executed operations from native execution records.
   - Preserve one parsed event per physical transcript row. Extend the existing activity projection so direct calls and matching completion records produce one execution, keyed by host, thread, and native call/item ID.
   - Preserve `ActivityLift` and existing command/file queries. Add native-origin metadata and a Rust-backed `TranscriptCursor.feed(bytes)` returning the current snapshot, earliest changed event index, and committed row count.
   - Reuse that cursor for watching and capt-hook’s transcript cache. Rebuild activity when normalization revises earlier events; retain immutable snapshots.
   - Correct native namespace handling, Codex child traversal, human-input waiting classification, `CODEX_HOME` resolution, and token accounting. Preserve exact native inputs where available; never manufacture replayable input from completion-only telemetry.

3. **Separate capt-hook’s shared engine from host protocols.**
   - Add explicit `--host claude|codex`; existing invocations retain Claude behavior. Adapters own input decoding, output encoding, event capabilities, transcript lookup, and installation.
   - Preserve `Event`, `@on`, conditions, and `HookResult`; add `PostCompact` and `Interrupt`. Separate result aggregation from Claude serialization at `captain_hook/dispatch.py:317#p6b2`.
   - Add `evt.file_reads` and `evt.file_changes`, using cc-transcript’s existing tool and patch types. Keep `evt.file` for singular native operations. Enumerate every patch change, including rename destinations.
   - Identify shell reads through existing command parsing and known command shapes. Only proven complete reads count toward reread suppression. Preserve one hook invocation and one combined decision per native tool call.
   - Round-trip rewrites through the original host payload. Reject unsupported event/action combinations explicitly; absence of a decision must retain the host’s default behavior.
   - Carry host, root session, agent/thread, and turn identity through the Python/Go protocol, state, logging, reviewer correlation, and helper UI. Isolate workers and registry caches by host, project, config home, and resolved plugin/tool registry.
   - Replace stateless transcript parsing at `captain_hook/daemon/transcache.py:135#z18e` with the shared cursor.
   - Keep existing Claude state locations for this rollout; give Codex a separate session namespace. Avoid an unrelated framework-wide state relocation.

4. **Add shared Codex session ownership and interactive delivery through cc-interact.**
   - Introduce a reusable Codex launcher/bridge in cc-interact, consumed by cc-present, cc-review, and cc-orchestrate.
   - Manage one loopback WebSocket app-server per effective `CODEX_HOME`, using the validated standalone Codex runtime. CLI and Orca terminals attach with `--remote`; desktop uses its existing `CODEX_APP_SERVER_WS_URL` support.
   - Bind interactions to `{host, account home, endpoint, thread ID, attach generation}`. Process IDs serve liveness only. Migrate existing cc-interact ownership records transactionally without discarding boards or reviews.
   - Deliver board events through `turn/start` with `toolOutput`, preserving tool provenance. Persist event cursors, include stable event IDs, reconcile replay, and reject stale attachment generations. This API queues output into active turns and can start processing on idle threads. [App Server](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server)
   - Strip terminal-specific environment from the shared server. The launcher records each thread’s Orca/cmux context; a context-restoring wrapper invokes the existing notification hooks.
   - Queue only terminal-notification startup invocations that arrive before binding, then replay after registration. Blocking and context-producing hooks remain synchronous.
   - Preserve cc-present’s renderer, board API, event log, and clients. Adapt its skill, triage delegation, component discovery, and session reattachment.

5. **Port the plugin fleet from shared sources.**
   - Keep source repositories and marketplace ownership intact. Add Codex packaging and host-specific launchers around shared CLI, MCP, skill, and hook-pack resources. Use owned overlays for third-party adaptations.
   - **ccx:** add host-aware MCP discovery using Codex’s structured inventory, host/project-sensitive caching, portable reader/reviewer procedures, and file-operation guards.
   - **ccn:** propagate Codex session provenance and project context; port recall, edit staleness, durable-record guidance, and compaction restoration.
   - **cc-guides:** protect generated files through normalized patch operations.
   - **cc-present, cc-review, cc-orchestrate:** share cc-interact’s ownership and feedback transport. Preserve cco’s existing child-fleet runtime selection; supporting Codex as its controller does not require changing every child runtime.
   - **Workflow plugins:** adapt `codex`, `show`, `getaway`, `wlm`, `repo-bootstrap`, `agent-browser-with-cookies`, `open-pr`, `long-running`, `design-doc`, and `incident-retro` to native Codex delegation, background work, and cc-present.
   - **Remaining packages:** preserve both slop-cop workflows, writing-docs, gh-profile, gen-image, llm-prompts, revdiff, Datadog, and applicable claudish behavior. Include gh-profile’s missing repo-summaries dependency.
   - Share agent procedure bodies through skills; generate thin Codex role definitions where named delegation is required. Do not copy Claude tool/model frontmatter.
   - Record two limits explicitly: no native port of the Claude rust-analyzer LSP declaration, and no guaranteed display-only assistant-message transform for claudish. Preserve Rust diagnostics/inspection and claudish’s explicit rewrite workflows.

6. **Wire and roll out the monorepo integration.**
   - Preserve `.agents/skills` as the existing shared source.
   - Move its five shared capt-hook definitions into `.capt-hook/hooks`, configure both hosts to load that directory, and preserve hook identities.
   - Port commit/PR formatting, unsafe job cleanup, unpublished-PR warnings, blocking-review warnings, and repeated-retry guidance.
   - Add project-scoped Codex configuration for these policies and the existing Linear/Sentry integrations. Preserve existing cmux/Orca hooks and unrelated user configuration.
   - Install compatible dependency builds and the matching signed Captain Hook helper, refresh plugin caches through supported commands, review changed hook trust definitions, and restart clients onto the shared server.

## Potential pitfalls

- Hook payloads and transcript tool records use different envelopes; correlate native IDs and normalize deliberately.
- Multi-file patches must not silently bypass singular-file guards or combine one file’s path with another file’s content.
- Transcript appends can revise prior normalized events; an append-only cache assumption is incorrect.
- Shared-server environment cannot identify the terminal owning a thread. Startup binding must avoid a launcher/hook deadlock.
- Desktop’s bundled runtime is older than the installed CLI. Successful attachment and feedback delivery are rollout gates.
- Plugin installation alone does not establish equivalent behavior or grant hook trust.

## Workflow plan

The main agent owns contracts, dependency pins, integration decisions, and reporting. Independent implementation uses isolated worktrees; reviews consume completed artifacts.

| Phase | Blocks on | Shape | Agents | Verification |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Matching baselines and fixtures | — | parallel | GPT-5.6-sol high ×2 | Inventory and reproducible payload fixtures |
| B: Transcript normalization/cursor | A | pipeline | GPT-6-astra high | Native/Python/Swift parity |
| C: Hook adapters and semantic operations | A; B for integration | parallel | GPT-6-astra high ×2 | Claude regression and Codex contract tests |
| D: Shared server and cc-interact transport | A | parallel | GPT-6-astra high | Ownership, delivery, restart tests |
| E: Shared skills and packaging | A | parallel | GPT-5.6-sol high ×2 | Manifest/resource validation |
| F: Behavioral plugin ports | B, C, D, E as consumed | parallel | GPT-6-astra high ×3 | Per-plugin acceptance matrix |
| G: Independent review | Each completed implementation | loop | GPT-5.6-sol high ×2 | Findings resolved and targeted retests |
| H: Monorepo rollout | F, G | pipeline | GPT-5.6-sol high | Three-surface smoke tests |

## Verification

Run the relevant package gates:

- **cc-transcript:** `uv run pytest`, `cargo test -p cc-transcript-core`, `cargo test -p cc-transcript-core --no-default-features`, `cargo test -p cc_transcript_swift`, `swift test --package-path swift`, and `uv build`; regenerate native/export stubs and affected goldens.
- **capt-hook:** `make`, including Python, Go race tests, tutorial parity, and Swift helper tests.
- **Modified Go packages:** `go test -race ./...` and `go vet ./...` in each repository.
- **Documentation:** `slop-cop check <file> --lang=markdown` for changed Markdown. Review each repository with `ccx vcs diff`.

Add end-to-end cases proving:

- Deny, context, and rewrite behavior for direct and nested shell/MCP calls; complete multi-file patches and renames.
- Incremental/full-parse equivalence across partial rows, late results, compaction, file replacement, and child sessions.
- Separate Claude/Codex sessions and multiple Codex threads sharing one server.
- cc-present comments reaching active and idle owning threads, with restart/replay handling and preserved tool provenance.
- Correct Orca/cmux notifications before and after startup binding.
- ccx/ccn behavior, every applicable plugin workflow, and all five monorepo policies across CLI, desktop, and Orca terminals.
